chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari narrated, saying: Abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari narrated to me, saying: I was with Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) at the time of the death of his son, Abu Ja'far, who had been indicated and pointed to by him. And I was reflecting in myself, saying: This is the story of Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and the story of Ismail. So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) turned to me and said: Yes, O Abu Hashim. God manifested (Bada) regarding Abu Ja'far and made Abu Ja'far and replaced his place with Abu Muhammad, just as He manifested regarding Ismail after Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had indicated him and appointed him. And it is as your soul told you, although the disbelievers dislike it. Abu Muhammad is my son, the successor after me; with him is what you need and with him is the instrument of Imamate, and praise be to God.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, son of Imam al-Askari
key_terms.بَدَا: Divine manifestation or change in decree

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Bada in the death of Imam al-Askari's son Abu Ja'far?
ai.summary: This hadith from Kitab al-Ghayba records the pivotal moment of the death of Imam al-Askari’s son, Abu Ja'far, and the subsequent divine manifestation (Bada) of his successor, Abu Muhammad (al-Mahdi). The Imam confirms that this change in designation is a preordained divine occurrence, analogous to the succession of Ismail after Ja'far, thereby ensuring the continuity of the Imamate despite the death of the previously indicated heir. This event serves as a crucial refutation of sects who doubted the legitimacy of the Mahdi due to the brief period of his father's son's life, affirming that the 'instrument of Imamate' remains with the designated successor regardless of apparent changes.
